Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Game Turn 2 Card Effects 3 Special Actions 4 Other Scoring Concepts 5 End of Game 6 Additional Information 6.1 Distribution of cards 6.1.1 Effect side: 6.1.2 Casino number side: Game Turn Flip 3 Casino cards - At the beginning of each turn, the card from the top of each stack is flipped and placed next to it, effect side up, creating three combinations: Casino number / Effect. Flipped cards will be stacked in three discarded stacks. Pick a number / effect combination - The players turn is simultaneous: each player individually picks one of the three combinations available and applies the results on their sheets. Several architects can therefore choose the same combination. Open a Casino (compulsory) - First, each architect must write the number of the combination they picked in the casino of one of their 4 streets on their city sheet. Numbers must always be written in an empty and constructed Casino, that is a casino without a crane or with a crossed off crane (see Construction effect page 8). They must be put in ascending order from left to right in each street independently. Note: If a player cannot write any of the 3 numbers of the Casino cards because they cannot respect the placement rules, they get to check 2 boxes on the Inauguration Track on their score sheet and will not be able to perform any action this turn. Perform the Effect (optional) - The player’s chosen combination allows them to perform an effect, if they wish, and if they have opened a casino with the Casino card. Important: an effect is always optional. Card Effects Inauguration (Scissors Cutting Ribbon) - Tick one circle on inauguration track. If the track is filled, game end is triggered. For every 2 circles filled, you can optionally use one of the 3 bonus actions. At game end, players count the number of inauguration spots filled. The player with most garners 1st place and scores the bonus points listed on their player sheet. Second and third place do the same. However, all players with the least inauguration spots filled encircle the debt marker on their sheet by the placement column. Limousine - Draw 2 segments for limousine path. Points or cash bundles are garnered toward game end for every red carpet on a finished casino passed by limousine. Points are deducted at game end for every segment needed to get back to the starting point. Construction (Crane) - Build a casino location, and circle the debt marker for that spot. Debt marker is crossed out if a casino is built over the newly constructed location. Improvement (Calculator) - Scratch over or fill in EXACTLY one of the multiplier boxes at the bottom of the screen of your player board (except for shows). The bottom most uncovered number will go toward your final score. Show Opening (Pink Star) - If placed on a casino with a star on its ceiling, then you can fill in one of the spots on the 2 columns of the show track of your player board. If a column is started, circle the 2 debt markers by that column. The debt marker can be crossed out if the circle next to it is filled. (i.e. you might not want to start a show if you don't think you can pay for the debt marker at the bottom) Special Actions For every 2 filled inauguration spots, you may use one of 3 bonus actions on your turn. Increase or decrease the number of your chosen cards by up to -2/-1/+1/+2. Cross out the debt marker above the inauguration pair when used. (i.e. No debt) Change the action of your chosen cards to one of the other 4 possible actions. Cross out the debt marker above the inauguration pair when used. [Rating: 1/10] (after a single play on BGA)  No matter how hard I tried, I just could not get all the rules for the different ways of scoring points into my head. It's not that I have a problem with complex games. But I suppose there has to be something about it to interest me and this doesn't.  I much prefer the original.

[Rating: 1/10] The direct sequel to 'Welcome To...' ends up being a poster boy for more not always being better. New Las Vegas ends up adding more details and mechanics than the original's foundation can cleanly handle.  Regardless of this game's ties to the original Welcome To- the fact remains that this is one of the least accessible filler games I have ever experienced.   Pros:  - Want 'Welcome to...' with denser mechanics? Well, this game went out of its way to serve you. And it MIGHT therefore satisfy you. Might. [Rating: 2/10] An unnecessarily complex twist on Welcome To..., adding all sorts of complicated new scoring systems to pursue. I can perhaps see this might be needed for people who have played the original 100+ times, but I hope that won't be me any time soon.

[Rating: 2/10] Welcome to is fantastic and easy to play and teach. This one was too complicated and it has too many things to take care of for me.

[Rating: 2/10] This game is nothing more than overly complicated, completely solitary, spreadsheet-optimization busywork. About half way into it I found myself wishing I had just sat it out. Easily the worst game I've played this year.

[Rating: 3/10] They tried to cram way too much on a framework that worked previously.  There are some decent ideas (the golf course is neat), but overall this is a bloated mess.

[Rating: 3/10] Played this after the whole Welcome To... hype but perhaps should've started with that one first. This one felt unnecessarily bloated.

[Rating: 3/10] Welcome To your kitchen sink, where we have thrown every game mechanic we can think of.

[Rating: 3/10] Like why? They have taken a decent game and just filled it to the brim with crap. No idea who asked for this.

[Rating: 3/10] Incredibly disappointing overall, some points:   - Higher complexity without enough payoff.  - Unclear rules around one of the mechanisms (Limo) - Easily possibly to block yourself and no resolution in the rules.  - I really like the golf course aspect, it's a nice variance contrasted against the other streets.  - I like that columns have an importance & value.  - The debt/money mechanism feels poorly executed - They should have added some tokens for this instead of staunchly sticking to pencil/paper.
